# Exact charge-sector Gaussian trajectory construction

29 October 2026. Root constructive extension of A's independently selected
positive Gaussian representation. Internal derivation; novelty and practical
superiority are UNESTABLISHED. This is an actual restricted noisy-system
simulation operation, not a noiseless many-body solver.

Let n=(n_1,...,n_m) be fermionic occupations and let

  H = H_0 + (1/2) n^T U n,
  L_Gamma(rho) = -(1/2) sum_ij Gamma_ij [n_i,[n_j,rho]],

with real symmetric U, real PSD physical Gamma, and number-conserving
quadratic H_0. More generally H_0 preserves diagonal charges C^T n.
The initial Gaussian state and all subsequent states are supported in a
single sector C^T n=q. C has linearly independent columns; Q has orthonormal
columns spanning ker(C^T). Charges must be genuinely preserved, not inferred
from a small mean or approximate conservation law.

For any real s and V, define

  U' = U + diag(s) + C V^T + V C^T.

On this sector, the added Hamiltonian is the quadratic operator
g^T n, g=s/2+Vq. Replace H_0 by H_0-g^T n. No interaction has been erased
outside the stipulated sector. On every sector coherence a,b,
C^T(a-b)=0, so dephasing only depends on Q^T Gamma Q.

Choose D=diag(d)>0 satisfying

  Q^T [Gamma - D - (1/4) U' D^-1 U'] Q >= 0.              (1)

This is sufficient for exact positive Gaussian trajectories of the
interaction-plus-dephasing channel at ANY finite time step. An equivalent
affine block LMI is

 [ Q^T(Gamma-D)Q     (1/2)Q^T U' ] >=0.                 (2)
 [ (1/2)U' Q                  D ]

Thus, for Gamma=gamma Gamma_0, finding a certificate and minimizing gamma
over d,s,V is an SDP, not a many-body state search. Strict d_i>0 is required
for this sampler; numerical optimization needs a positive floor and slack.
We do not claim (1) is necessary for all possible Gaussian decompositions.

## Explicit finite-step instrument and proof

For a step h>0, use reference measure y~N(0,h I) and the positive diagonal
measurement operator

 M_y = exp[sum_i (sqrt(d_i)y_i - h d_i)n_i].

Its squared average is I because n_i^2=n_i, so it is a normalized instrument.
Follow it by the Gaussian phase feedback

 F_y = exp[-i (1/2) n^T U' D^-1/2 y].

For occupations a,b, let delta=a-b and v=a+b. Gaussian integration gives

 E[(F_y M_y)_aa conj((F_y M_y)_bb)]
 = exp[-ih/2(a^T U'a-b^T U'b)
       -h/2 delta^T (D+(1/4)U'D^-1U') delta]

GENERAL FINITE-STEP CHARGE-SECTOR GAUSSIAN INSTRUMENT
29 October 2026. Root internally supported construction; not yet independently
accepted; priority and useful runtime advantage unestablished.

This strictly generalizes the positive-diagonal measurement ansatz in
CONSTRUCTION.md at the level of allowed parameters. Whether it strictly
enlarges the feasible physical-noise set is an investigation, not assumed.

Retain H=.5 n^T U n+H0, physical dephasing Gamma PSD, and EXACT preserved
sector C^T n=q. Choose real symmetric X,Y,U' obeying

 X = diag(d)+C Vx^T+Vx C^T,
 U'= U+diag(s)+C Vu^T+Vu C^T,
 Q^T(X+Y)Q=Q^T Gamma Q,

              [ X       -U'/2 ] >=0.                       (G1)
              [ -U'/2       Y ]

There is no sign restriction on d. The covariance itself imposes X,Y PSD.
All these constraints are affine, hence minimize gamma with Gamma=gamma
Gamma0 by SDP. Singular X is permitted, so no artificial positive floor.
Let l=d+2Vx q and g=s/2+Vu q. Within the fixed sector n^T X n=l^T n and
.5 n^T(U'-U)n=g^T n.

FINITE-STEP IDENTITY. Under a reference JOINT REAL Gaussian law (a,b) with
mean zero and covariance h [[X,-U'/2],[-U'/2,Y]], use Kraus operator

       K_(a,b)=exp[(a+i b)^T n - h l^T n].                 (G2)

On an occupation coherence between r,t in the sector, let delta=r-t and
v=r+t. Integrating K_rr conjugate(K_tt) gives

 exp[-ih/2(r^T U'r-t^T U't)
     +h/2 v^T X v-h l^T v-h/2 delta^T Y delta]
 =exp[-ih/2(r^T U'r-t^T U't)-h/2 delta^T(X+Y)delta].     (G3)

The equality follows from r^T Xr=l^T r, t^T Xt=l^T t. The quadratic gauge
correction -g^T n in H0 and Q^T noise identity recover the target channel.
On diagonals r=t, (G3)=1, establishing trace preservation ON THE SECTOR.
Each K is a fermion Gaussian operator; no nonlinear state approximation.
The covariance need not define a trace-preserving instrument off-sector.

1. Sample an auxiliary occupation configuration s from diag(rho) of the
   CURRENT Gaussian trajectory, using ordinary determinantal point process
   sampling (or Gaussian occupation sampling). This is an auxiliary random
   variable; DO NOT replace the trajectory state by that configuration.

EXACT OPTIMIZATION OF THE DECLARED GAUSSIAN-EXPONENTIAL CONE
29 October 2026. Root construction; independent review pending.

The larger cone in GENERAL_CONE.txt did not improve the first random8
or Hadamard16 diagnostic. This is explained analytically, rather than
funding more covariance optimization.

For physical dephasing Gamma=gamma I and fixed charges C^T n=q, define

 alpha(U,C)= min_s ||Q^T [U+diag(s)] Q||_op,              (O1)

where Q is any orthonormal basis of ker(C^T). Within the declared
Gaussian-exponential covariance cone (G1), the minimum gamma is EXACTLY
alpha(U,C). This is a characterization of that ansatz, not all positive
Gaussian decompositions, all classical simulators, or quantum dynamics.

NECESSITY. In any feasible covariance matrix, test the vectors (Qx,Qx)
and (Qx,-Qx). The two nonnegative quadratic forms imply

 x^T Q^T (X+Y +/- U') Q x >=0.

Projected X+Y equals gamma I and projected U' equals U+diag(s), since
the charge gauge vanishes there. Hence
 -gamma I <= Q^T[U+diag(s)]Q <= gamma I.
Taking the smallest possible s proves gamma>=alpha.

SUFFICIENCY AND ACTUAL CONSTRUCTION. Given s and gamma satisfying the
last two inequalities, put P=QQ^T and A=U+diag(s), and choose

 U'=PAP, X=Y=gamma I/2.

Then U'-A is a charge gauge CV^T+VC^T, because its quadratic restriction
to ker(C^T) is zero. One explicit formula, with G=C^T C, is

 V=-(A C)G^-1 + (1/2) C G^-1(C^T A C)G^-1,
 U'=A+CV^T+VC^T.

Block rotation by (I,I)/sqrt(2) and (I,-I)/sqrt(2) transforms covariance
[[gamma I/2,-U'/2],[-U'/2,gamma I/2]] into
(gamma I-U')/2 and (gamma I+U')/2, both PSD. The explicit sampler in
GENERAL_CONE.txt therefore applies, with simple real covariance X.
Use quadratic Hamiltonian correction g=s/2+Vq as before.

O1 is a smaller SDP with m variables s, gamma and TWO (m-r)-square LMIs.
No trajectory or exponential-size state is searched. A minimizer exists:
the image of s in the finite-dimensional symmetric-matrix space is a
closed linear subspace; minimizing norm over an affine subspace attains
its distance. An arbitrary representation of s can be chosen if its
kernel causes nonuniqueness. Singular covariance is permitted at equality.

POSITIVE NONUNIFORM LOCAL NOISE. More generally Gamma=gamma G0 for known
positive DIAGONAL G0. The exact criterion in the same ansatz is existence
of s such that

 Q^T [gamma G0 +/- (U+diag(s))] Q >=0.
